one_line: A browser-based money-planning workspace that lets ChatGPT explain forecasts and stage bounded savings recommendations for approval.
what_it_does: Tracks balances, income, bills, goals, minimum-balance limits, and forecasts, with an agent-assisted recommendation flow that requires human approval and applies only the exact approved recommendation.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to current financial state, invalidation of stale approvals, and exact-once bounded application make the agent materially safer and more reliable than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies page-scoped WebMCP reads of current workspace state.
Agent cannot approve; user approval is required and only the exact recommendation can be applied once.
Changed balances, bills, goals, or limits cancel old approvals.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets show a coherent finance dashboard, forecast visualization, chat panel, workspace creation, and analysis-oriented flow, but no completed recommendation approval is visibly shown.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets visibly show CashLab-branded dashboard and three-step flow: tell basics, ask ChatGPT, approve recommendation.
Frames show balance, bills, savings goals, stepped forecast chart, tooltips, and conversational explanations.
No end-to-end applied recommendation is visible.
impact_rationale: Budgeting and cash-flow planning are concrete needs, and the product addresses the trust problem of letting an assistant reason over changing finances without granting it unilateral authority.
impact_evidence: Description identifies balances, bills, savings goals, and minimum-balance planning.
Forecast and recommendation review are visibly represented in the UI.
Human approval and local-records-only caveat bound the financial risk.
creativity_rationale: Conversational financial planning paired with stale-state invalidation and exact bounded approval is a thoughtful synthesis beyond a generic chatbot dashboard.

Approval is invalidated when relevant financial state changes.

usability_note: The staged setup and chart-plus-chat layout look understandable, though the evidence does not show the full approval flow.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame evidence shows setup and analysis but not completed application.
standouts: Strong safety boundary around consequential financial recommendations.

advance_reason: Strong WebMCP leverage and credible finance use case, with coherent visual evidence despite the missing end-to-end result.

one_line: An asymmetric co-op arcade game where a human operates a console and an AI reader uses WebMCP-held manuals to guide them.
what_it_does: Creates timed multi-act gameplay with information asymmetry, human-only controls, scoped per-act tools, communication, strikes, and bounded consequential actions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the game’s central wall between two players: typed scoped manual access creates the information asymmetry and collaboration that UI-driving or screen scraping would undermine.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly makes WebMCP the boundary between human operator and AI reader.
Each act registers scoped tools with AbortSignal and removes them when the act ends.
Human controls remain human-owned while the reader receives procedures, charts, codebooks, clock, and text channel.
execution_rationale: The packet and frame sheets coherently show the game premise, role separation, timed console, and interaction states; the exact win flow is not fully visible but the core product is convincingly evidenced.
execution_evidence: Frames show TALK FAST messaging, operator/reader roles, mode controls, and a timed game console.
Frames visibly show countdown states, status indicators, and console-like gameplay.
Description specifies ten minutes, three strikes, five acts, and attributed failures.
impact_rationale: It offers credible entertainment and a useful practice arena for human-agent delegation, with a clear audience despite being intentionally niche.
impact_evidence: Description identifies an asymmetric co-op arcade game for one human and one AI reader.
It also frames the experience as a practice arena for delegation and communication.
creativity_rationale: Making the WebMCP boundary itself the core asymmetric game mechanic is unusually original and pursued deeply through roles, scoped tools, and attributed strikes.
creativity_evidence: Neither player can win alone because each has complementary information/capability.
Tool visibility changes with game state.
Consequential override and fair-play caveat are explicitly designed into the game.
usability_note: The role model and visible timed console communicate the play loop, though multiplayer/agent onboarding details are not fully shown.
red_flags: The page cannot technically prevent an agent from viewing the screen; fair play relies on the intended typed path and captured record.
standouts: WebMCP is not a bolt-on; it is the information-asymmetry mechanic.

advance_reason: Most distinctive packet: WebMCP is indispensable to the game’s core mechanic, with strong visual and conceptual evidence.
